I was wondering about that. My guess is that Maya was an anomaly. She was supposed to be reset along with everyone but for some reason it failed, making it so only Maya was left instead of Sensei. (I think what happened was Sensei gave Maya his ability to reset the world after sakai's death.) When this happened it put him on auto pilot and made him live those years without gaining memory(making him "loose" what he did). My guess is that auto pilot disengaged for a couple years due to a malfunction. At this time it sent Pareidolia away from Sensei in the winter, meaning that he was unable to communicate with sensei. Auto pilot then re-engaged and once it was summer again a couple (non loop)years later when Sensei was sleeping it disengaged once more due to Ami(seeing as she has the power to do this). On Maya's side of things she found Pareidolia who helped her come up with a plan. The other two gods so far ended up breaking Sensei which she no longer trusted. Pareidolias plan was surefire but came with a consequence- Maya would never be able to love Sensei again. He told her if she ever mentioned love to sensei without Pareidolia re entering sensei, then he would not be able to protect the ones she loves. Maya then over the thousands of resets that she went through not being able to get auto pilot off but gaining enough distance from Sensei while showing Ami to be a friend, was able to let Ami let her guard down and turn auto pilot off. Once that happend she waited and waited until she was sure Pareidolia was able to get to Sensei(which was the fifth reset.) Ami found out however and played dumb making Maya let her guard down enough. Ami knew that Pareidolia would get Sensei off of auto pilot if sensei had the will to live. Ami then found out that sensei loved Maya and really put two and two together. During the holloween party she or whatever god she was talking to artificially started a reset which is why Maya was unable to detect it. She hated the gods but trusted Pareidolia even if his methods were evil. She talked to Pareidolia one last time before getting ready to be reset. They had sex and then Pareidolia mocked her for not realizing that Ami found out. Until v0.37 which we have no idea on what's gonna happen so my prediction is that Pareidolia will wait until Ami goes to get out and a)take control of Sensei to get him out or b) he will wake sensei up by either scolding him awake or tell him that he has a new mission of sorts which is to get Maya prime back telling him that the chances are near impossible but not entirely impossible. I think option a is more likely due to this being the saddest chapter but in not the next reset but the one after or the one after that he will find Maya. The next reset would be the perfect place for Sensei to fully get his will back, while giving Pareidolia his main spotlight as well.

Eh, based off how Pareidolia has acted in Chapter 4 so far, I wouldn't consider it the least Callous. Calling Maya Prime a bitch:
Pareidolia - "Frankly, that girl had it coming for being such an incorrigible, single-minded bitch all the time."
Mocking Sensei:
Pareidolia - "Stray cat got your tongue?"
- "You're supposed to smile, idiot."
- "What you're not supposed to do is sit there quietly and attempt to think. All that will do is detract from your purpose and trick you into believing you're worth more than you are."
- "Who's going to want to fuck you if all you can do is sit there and feel sorry for yourself? Because I'll be damned if you turn my chapter into some sappy, abstinent romp through an ocean of your tears."
- "do you have any idea how hard i had to work to get here? how long i had to wait? because i can guarantee you it would make the watermelon girl look like a tadpole gobbled up by it's mother frog."

Sensei is also being called a crybaby and little bitch in the background image.
And implying if he doesn't straighten up, Pareidolia will take more from him:
Pareidolia - "Or perhaps I need to take something else from you to spur you back to action?"

A Narrator even seemed scared of Pareidolia, yet still seemed to go behind it's back, risking themself to warn Sensei that God is using him:
Narrator - "I have disregarded the letter from the desk of the ninth god. And I have pulled the plug on AUTO-PILOT as I know from experience that wires can only do so much. Pareidolia will have my throat for it, but it will all be worthwhile if the two of US return to form."

Ami (?) - "Shut them out. Shut them out and listen to me. Because God is real, but God won't protect you. God wants to use you. And if you let him do that, it's all over."

Auto Pilot - "AUTO-PILOT has been reactivated and will proceed with narration as the host has been deemed 'unfit' to think for himself."
This Narrator may have even been The Shapeshifter, albeit it's not clear.

Meanwhile, the so called Callous god has casually healed Sensei just because it could:
Sensei - "It heals my wounds in an act of mercy."

Frankly, I've wondered it for awhile but perhaps Pareidolia has fucked up which god is which. Manipulated the perception of things. In other words: The Concerned god aka Pareidolia may actually be the Callous god, while The Callous god aka HOPE, Yasu's god, etc, is the true Concerned god.

That's a whole other can of worms that could change so much, though.

Click to expand...
To sum up my reasoning for Pareidolia's relation to Frogs and Spiders:

If you go back to Reset 4 in the 'A Life of Prizes' Main Event in Chapter 2, you'll find a book that corresponds to each god and each C word based off a survey you would have taken in the 'A Spotless Mind' Chapter 2 Main Event.

This book changes, depending on which C you choose, from Callous to Calm to Concerned in this order which leads to these books:
If you chose Callous you'd get the "Book 9: The Lust Eater"
If you chose Calm you'd get the "Book 9: The Wire God"
If you chose Concerned you'd get the "Book 9: The Dark"
This seems to be where Pareidolia's "The Dark" title was revealed, and is probably why last update, it's talking about beautiful things emerging from the dark:
Pareidolia - "beautiful things emerge from the dark, AKIRA."
(It's referring to itself apparently, and Sensei probably doesn't fully understand that)

Anyway, in Book 9: The Dark, Pareidolia talks to you, but before that, Sensei describes the book in a way that presumably describes the god:
Sensei - "I open up a book that begins to crumble upon being touched."
- "It looks as if it's been haphazardly pieced together with different parts of other books and pages of all different sizes."
- "From out of the pages crawls a small spider that finds its way onto my hand."
With The Dark's book specifically referencing a spider, it might make something else seem impossible to ignore.

Kaori is both The Mistress of The Dark and The Queen of Spiders:
Kaori - "Yes! That is what I am called. But you may also address me as the Mistress of the Dark or the Queen of Spiders. All of these things are true! I think!"
The correlation here seems a little uncanny.

Not to mention, Pareidolia's aka The Concerned's weakness and haphazardness implied by Book 9: The Dark, also fits Kaori, as she has a weak spot and a seemingly messed up mind and body that doesn't seem entirely hers or functional.

Anyway, now besides the Giant Frog at the Pareidolia Mall, Pareidolia actually called Maya a tadpole being eaten by it's mother frog in last updates 'On the Count of Three' Chapter 4 Main Event:
Pareidolia- "do you have any idea how hard i had to work to get here? how long i had to wait? because i can guarantee it would make the watermelon girl look like a tadpole gobbled up by its mother frog. which, without beating around the bush, is kind of what she is in the first place. well...was. whoops."
Which definitely leads credence to Maya being related to an Egg from a Frog, since Pareidolia implies she kind of was a tadpole at least.

The Giant Frog, and this strange metaphor(?) about a Mother Frog aside, at the end of Last Update in the 'Miserably Ever After' Chapter 4 Main Event, we have Kaori, who seems related to Pareidolia, giving Nao-chan a Frog as a Christmas present:
Auto Pilot - "'Nao-chan' pets a small frog that was given to her as her very first Christmas present."

Taking into account the Kaori/Pareidolia stuff prior, then this small frog given to Nao-chan, may not actually be as random as it would seem.

Overall: This is why I say it seems Spiders and Frogs are related to Pareidolia.

The cover leaves me thinking more about the symbolism with the insects and associates in Lil, since there is also the symbolism with flowers for each girl and birds.
Since there are spiders, although they are not insects, they eat them, and they are associated with several girls in the story, there are also termites in happy event, worms and tapeworms in other parts ((reminds me of the theory of how tapeworm and bucket of a happy event related to Hope, and Moyo)),
there are also the flatworm guineas in that way, which are the ones associated with the Rin's wounds on her arms
Cockroaches in a lot of happy events, and here he comes back and they come out almost in an army
and also butterflies as accessories on several girls, Sekai, Imani, Ami
Then there are the fireflies used in some romantic or emotional moments of the game like Maya's, final beach event
There may be a little more but that's what comes to mind the most.
but the praying mantis is new if my memory serves, and they are those where after having sex to procreate, the female eats the male, which is not random, and seeing Sekai in parts of other places, with that the first thing What would come to my mind would be maybe a new happy event, or the last Main Events come loaded with internal struggles and symbolism of his trauma in Akira's mind.

((and by the way the female Mantis is by quantities of size several times larger than the Male, which reinforces in other words the Groomin abuse of Sekai Female Praying Mantis towards Male Praying Mantis Akira))

Another way to interpret it is: The Serpent revealed to Eve that God lied that the Tree of Knowledge would kill them if they ate from it, and just didn't want them to be like God. God then punished and banished them, so that they wouldn't be immortal, on top of being like God, due to now knowing the reality of things.

Eden is probably Kumon-Mi and God is probably Pareidolia (or any god). Eve might be Maya and Adam is probably Sensei. Something woke up Maya, and Maya tried to wake up Sensei, like how Eve fed Adam the fruit.

Ami (?) - "Shut them out. Shut them out and listen to me. Because God is real, but God won't protect you. God wants to use you. And if you let him do that, it's all over."
Could be overthinking things though.

posts.content_html_raw:
I loved this update! Akira’s finally up and around, and even though he’s extremely depressed, I’m so glad to see him finally showing some real emotion.

As much as I wanted to slap Ami for her obsessiveness, by the end, I couldn’t help but feel a little bad for her. She’s obviously broken, herself, and is dealing with a lot of trauma. Here’s hoping Akira can step up to the plate and try his best for Ami as her guardian.

Another interesting thing was Maya’s reaction to Ami’s speech in the classroom. She seemed quite angered by her words, and Ayane’s earlier explanation regarding her bell leads me to believe she just might still love Akira after all… Only time will tell, though.

I have no clue what the choice between the two Wizards will mean, but I just hope I made the right choice. I went with Tsukasa, simply because it felt like a safer bet than Chinami.

That flashback with Wizard Maya and Noriko during their tutoring caught me so off guard in the best possible way! Shit had me emotional, man… I love peering into the past like that. What makes it even better is both Maya and Noriko are two of my favorite characters in the game. I mean, just look at my signatures!

What else can I say? Sana’s H scene was pretty solid, and I’m intrigued by how her change in character will evolve moving forward. More of Rin is always a good thing! I’m surprised yet not surprised she stayed to listen in on Akira and Sana at the Halloween Party.

Osako’s events were fairly decent, but were more setup for future updates. And I think we alllll know what for.

Soooo yeah! Banger of an update! Can’t wait for next month to see what happens next.

posts.content_html_raw:
Highlight of the event for me was the bants with Osako. The writing felt very chapter 1 or 2 in a way I've been missing lately. I was also brought back around on Ami after quite a few updates of not really liking her. The way she snapped back to lucidity after stabbing Akira made my heart sink. I look forward to seeing where the story goes with her.
My only complaint is a lack of Maya, and yes I know there's an obvious reason for it but Akira's reaction to the letter gave me false hope and I can't help but be a little let down a tiny bit that we have to wait (at least) one more update to get that ball rolling along. Also I think Chika knowing about the other girls' nudes should have lead to something more immediately. I know it's safe to assume it will come back at some point, but I at this point really want literally anything new to happen with Chika, whether it 's a genuine loosening of the leash or a full on tipping point where she can no longer keep her head in the sand, and I think with how immediately crazy she's been in the past over much more minor stuff, it feels like she only didn't flip out so that the wizard plot can move forward.
All in all I had a lot more fun than I was expecting, and I'm glad to see selly hasn't lost the touch for well written, lightly comedic banter. I'm excited for character interactions moving forward with the new status quo.

Good update. I am sooo glad the story kept moving somewhat as I was really worried after playing the generic events. I thought "how is this sorry ass excuse of a man going to carry the story now" and the answer was: by the girls forcing him to it until he can pick it up himself. Good. He was a total pushover this update (other than facing Ami) but I'm not complaining. We got the best scenario: a more expresive Akira without dragging the story down. Thank you so much Sel!

I'm also glad the Sana's arc continued immediately after christmass instead of having to wait after a chunk of updates llike happened in the past with other big events. Not sure if the date of her birthday was intentional... It makes sense she finally unwraps that very big present on her birthday but there was no reference to it otherwise. I can see the girls not knowing about it, but I imagine Sara would throw the ultimate party for her and she did nothing?

The only thing stopping a Chika/Rin/Akira threesome now is that promise Selebus made that we will be able to have the 100% of events in a single playthrough. Hoping he breaks it. Also, The Rin/Sara pairing is interesting and Selebus went out of his way with a very contrived plot device to make it happen. Must be something there and reinforce the theory that Rin is Sana's half sister.

Yumi working in the convenience store always made the more sense, IIRC we have events of her coming now so i guess that is what we'll see next update. She having "her own place" now means that Sensei can visit her without Chika roaming around which only increase the possibility of something happening sooner rather than later. Noice.

More Yumi and more Wakana is very needed.

Wizard content could also come sooner than we thought. Looking forward to more of those flashbacks. And for good or bad, I'm on Tsukasa's team.

Take your time Ami. You don't want to rush it and get up before you are ready to go out, okay? Follow the advice you gave to your uncle, it was a very good one.

Gotta say, the most surprising part of this update is that Sensei actually:
Defended his niece somewhat for once:
Sensei - "I don't think that will be necessary. She did a great job, all things considered."
- "Ami's taken care of me the entire time and I don't want any of you holding that against her as that's what I would have wanted her to do if I was...you know. Conscious."
- "And she did a great job, I think. Even if it meant dissapointing or angering any of you who may have wanted to come visit me."
Ami - "And by 'probably' I mean you should definitely leave him alone because A --- you don't get it. And B --- you just want him to fuck your silly little brains out! Teehee!"
Sensei - "Better than you can, at least. And I really hate saying that after everything I just saw her say to you and everyone else, but she's right about one thing --- you guys don't get it."

Even saying he's proud of her:

Sensei - "I know you're doing all you can. And I'm very proud of you for that. I mean it."

The rest was somewhat predictable, but that was a little surprising.

We'll just have to wait and see how long this new "purpose" of his lasts, though.

posts.content_html_raw:
Haven't had an update quite like this for a long time that makes you feel like progress was made in plenty of directions with pleasant surprises at many corners, good stuff.

The only little dissatisfaction I have is not having a chance to converse with Makoto about the recent development, and not having a Touka event immediately after acquiring her number to see her shell cracking, but it's fine these can wait.

- Apparent Ami figured out Sensei's passcode within that 2 months to be able to check his messages, or she just knows the code the whole time without him knowing that.

(RIP anyone who's sent him nudes or inappropriate content)

- Something that caught my attention is the exact same dialogue used in Mother's milk between Sekai and teen Akira, and in Episcopalis between Akira and teen Maya. I don't know what this can be insinuating, similarity between these two unspeakable relationship? Similarity between Sekai and Maya? the passive role of Akira in these two relationship?



- Apparently with the right stimulus, Akira can recollect his own tutoring time memory by himself without dying or resetting like Maya alluded to. Though the part he recovered is only the exceedingly normal part, this kinda further proves that Maya previously believing bringing up the past would kill him isn't correct (granted, a lot has changed in ch4, both his mind and the god in control. So this comparison might not be properly).

- Finally, I LOVE the amount of interactions with our lovely adults. Wakana is pleasantly surprising, Osaka is just plain awesome, but I think what moves me is when Rika says “Yo cut this crap do you still want to be friends? cause we’re all down if you are; ain’t nobody asking if you’re a bad individual or not you’re missing the point goober!” This I think is really sweet, gotta love these Rokuharas.

Maya - "Sometimes, forcing people to do things they're not comfortable with is the best way to move them forward."
Sensei - "Because sometimes, forcing people to do things they're not comfortable with is the best way to move them forward."
- "There's a pair of scissors on the desk that whispers this to me in a voice I'd rather forget."
This update.

Sensei - "I mean...it's definitely frustrating. But there's no point forcing anyone to do anything they don't want to do."
Maya - "I think there's someone who would be very upset to hear you say that."
That someone she mentions was probably herself.

posts.content_html_raw:
Some food for thought
During Ami's delirium in Della, she said something that doesn't simply come from trapping in bedtime story hallucination and/or a fit of anger.

Why haven't you kept playing BREED YOUR NIECE MINI GAME?!?!?!
Ami has always been a prime suspect of time fuckery-related matters or basically anything unexplainable, but it also has always been hard to really tell how much she knows and/or how much she's involved. This time, however, these lines aren't delivered during resets, happy events, or dreamy sequences to confuse or shock players; she delivers these words diegetically to Sensei.

So, does she in fact know A LOT MORE than she lets on? Does she also know about the reincarnation, but have an opinion on the complete opposite side of Maya?

Or, Is Ami during Della in a god-induced blackout and something other than Ami was scolding us through Ami?

Or, since Ami recites parts of conversation she and Sensei had back in A New You, perhaps after finding out "his brain being stupid" and how similar the situation was compared to a manga or a game, Ami from that point forward started treating things really like a game (a porn game no less) and wished Sensei to do the same so that her envisioned future of being with her uncle is no longer impossible?

Personally, I think Ami subjectively wanting Sensei to treat this like a game so that she has a chance to end with him is the most straightforward take. But things are a lot spicier, much more interesting, and still explainable if she really knows more. Especially, I think getting Ami pregnant "should" have some otherworldly effects solely because events like Am I Awake exist, as if that event foreshadows what "her epilogue" looks like, or perhaps foreshadows how all the other Senseis who immediately slept with Ami ended.

fdsasdf_p said:
So, does she in fact know A LOT MORE than she lets on? Does she also know about the reincarnation, but have an opinion on the complete opposite side of Maya?
Click to expand...
Personally? I think she knows everything. Almost literally. I think she understands everything more than Maya ever has. It's clear she knows about the reset and it's nuances, as shown in that one even where she blatantly pretends to do the dialogue loop thing after being called on it. I think the only gaps in her understanding come from her not having access to stuff only sensei knows and sees, like the gods, Sekai, etc. Oh and she probably doesn't know the rules about how Maya couldn't (or can't?) get closer to sensei.
I think the reason she gets murderous whenever Maya tried to clue her in on the resets in the past was to maintain her perfect paradise that is the timeloop, and the fact she never killed Maya in one of those outbursts seems like a pretty clear warning to me.

Slightly more out on a limb: I think Ami is one of the keys to understanding, and ending, the resets, and I think she knows that too. My grand unified theory is that Sensei killed himself by jumping off the roof, and the loop was created when Maya, in an act of desperation, prayed for him back and/or things to go back to normal, and the supernatural forces that have always been in Kumon Mi (As I think is pretty definitively shown with Sara and Yasu. No I don't think they were just schizophrenic before the loops, the game goes out of it's way to show the opposite actually) granted her wish in a very Monkey's paw sort of way, hence the Vega parable she tells during the festival date. And I think Ami knows the loops revolve around Maya and Sensei, which is probably another source of murderous rage and how broken she is in general.

fdsasdf_p said:
Some food for thought
During Ami's delirium in Della, she said something that doesn't simply come from trapping in bedtime story hallucination and/or a fit of anger.
View attachment 3324363
Why haven't you kept playing BREED YOUR NIECE MINI GAME?!?!?!
Ami has always been a prime suspect of time fuckery-related matters or basically anything unexplainable, but it also has always been hard to really tell how much she knows and/or how much she's involved. This time, however, these lines aren't delivered during resets, happy events, or dreamy sequences to confuse or shock players; she delivers these words diegetically to Sensei.

So, does she in fact know A LOT MORE than she lets on? Does she also know about the reincarnation, but have an opinion on the complete opposite side of Maya?

Or, Is Ami during Della in a god-induced blackout and something other than Ami was scolding us through Ami?

Or, since Ami recites parts of conversation she and Sensei had back in A New You, perhaps after finding out "his brain being stupid" and how similar the situation was compared to a manga or a game, Ami from that point forward started treating things really like a game (a porn game no less) and wished Sensei to do the same so that her envisioned future of being with her uncle is no longer impossible?

Personally, I think Ami subjectively wanting Sensei to treat this like a game so that she has a chance to end with him is the most straightforward take. But things are a lot spicier, much more interesting, and still explainable if she really knows more. Especially, I think getting Ami pregnant "should" have some otherworldly effects solely because events like Am I Awake exist, as if that event foreshadows what "her epilogue" looks like, or perhaps foreshadows how all the other Senseis who immediately slept with Ami ended.
Click to expand...
Based off how Ami uncontrollably repeats things from Chapter 1 in Chapter 4:

Ami Chapter 1 - "Class ended ten minutes ago. It's time to get up."
Chapter 4 - "Class ended ten minutes ago. It's time to get up."
C1 - "So, allow me to re-introduce you to Kumon-mi! A super normal town just outside of Tokyo."
C4 - "Allow me to re-introduce you to Kumon-mi! A super normal town just outside of Tokyo."
C1 - "Rule number one is keep your hands off all of your students! But that should probably be a rule that goes without saying since...you know."
C4 - "Rule number one is keep your hands off all of your students! But that should probably be a rule that goes without saying since...you know."
C1 - "Well, you should. That's the part where you were supposed to say, 'You're the only girl for me, Ami! I don't care about any of the other ones!'"
C4 - "That's the part where you were supposed to say, 'You're the only girl for me, Ami! I don't care about any of the other ones!'"

I think it's far more likely that like how Tsuneyo, Makoto, and other girls tend to vaguely recall things they shouldn't, Ami does and has been as well. She probably recalls saying these exact words hundreds of thousands of times to hundreds of thousands of Sensei's somehow.

She's also mentioned stuff like Ayane isn't supposed to be here:
Ami - "But you're not. You're here. And I'm having a little trouble understanding how that could possibly be a good thing for any of us or why it's even happening in the first place."
Like an NPC suddenly moving where they shouldn't.

Considering how broken Ami is, she's probably just assumed this messed up world was actually a video game, just like how Chapter 1 Sensei treated everything like a game. Characters in a video game acting different all of a sudden has to be a little worrying for her.

Even Makoto seems to be thinking the same thing lately, and so like with most games, they just assumed this game has a specific goal. Being with Sensei.

Although, keep in mind that Ami mentioned talking with God this update:
Ami - "There are a million girls trying to trick you into believing we're not meant to be together, but I have talked to God and he says that we are."
And it's been established that she's been hearing voices for who knows how long:
Sensei - "Probably just the voices inside of your head or something."
Ami - "I don't think so. Those are a lot less reserved."

So, on top of being mentally ill, orphaned and traumatized, surrounded by shitty friends and a pathetic uncle, and trapped in some kind of chronoprison where she gets apparently butchered and her memories screwed with, sometimes she may have actual beings whispering things into her ears.

I think Maya is more in the sphere of Nodoka fucked up. If things go in that direction, I expect blackmail and really scummy manipulation.

posts.content_html_raw:
Seeing Yumi in the preview reminds me of something that I still don't quite get the logic behind after all these months: the infamous yumiknows flag.

This flag represents how much Yumi knows about Chika's relationship with Sensei (more specifically, Chika self-proclaiming to be his girlfriend), and determines her action at the end of Matador.

But to me, yumiknows at best can only represent whether she knows or not by the time of the event Abyss, and Yumi would still have tons of chances to learn it from Chika off-screen afterwards, in the same manner as Route A (IIRC there wasn't a specific event that entails Chika telling Yumi).
So in order to make Route B work, Yumi would have to remain completely oblivious throughout the time from Abyss all the way to Matador.

Since there really isn't anything that prevents Chika from telling Yumi off-screen, the fact that Chika apparently just decided not to say anything to Yumi if Abyss came first is what I find odd.
(note that there is no dialogue variation in Zanzibar that checks yumiknows, so Chika should have the same amount of tendency to tell Yumi regardless of routes)

It's not entirely confirmed, but it seems likely that Sekai hates Maya for one major reason:
  • Maya broke Sensei beyond repair, after the Accident.
Noriko reveals a lot about Maya, but one of the major things is how she believes Maya fucked Sensei up for good:
Noriko - "No, what I should have done is never let you take advantage of him. Because that fucked him up for good. And I think you know it."

As far as has been revealed, Maya was the one who pursued the relationship with Sensei:
Presumably Maya - "do you remember the first time you told me you loved me? it was snowing. i was wearing a green scarf. i confessed my feelings to you weeks prior and you had been sitting on your decision ever since. when you uttered those words, it was like my heart stopped. like everything i've ever wanted was finally mine. and i could finally be happy. you took me to your room and took my panties off. you put your fingers inside me and i started crying. but they were happy tears - because I finally knew what it meant to be loved."

We also had Pareidolia seemingly disliking Maya for how she groomed Sensei:
Pareidolia - "Not the person she wanted you to be. Not the person she groomed you into --- a broken man incapable of dividing what little love he has left into boxes to share with everyone and everything."

And we know that Maya tried to keep those that loved Sensei away from him, apparently convincing him he was all alone:
Noriko - "What you don't do is hide them from everyone else who cares about them and make them think they're all alone! That is being obsessed, Maya!"
Maya - "You should thank me for keeping her away as long as I have."
Sensei - "How were you the one who kept her away?"
Maya - "That doesn't concern you."

We also had Sensei mentioning he was willing to be Maya's toy last update:
Ami - "Maya never cared about you. And she never will care about you because she's a filthy liar who manipulates people into doing what she wants them to do. Plus, she-"
- "Plus, she's changed a lot these last couple months. I guess her true colors are really coming out now that her favorite toy has been taken away."
Sensei - "I will be a toy if it means..."
Ami - "You will do nothing of the sort. Your brain is going haywire right now and you're saying things you don't mean. But that's my fault for leaving you alone in a place where people can find you."

And, Ami has brought up that she suspects something must have hurt Sensei to cause him to stop tutoring:
Ami - "I'm sure it's not true, but I keep thinking that maybe something happened with you while I wasn't around that hurt you really bad."
- "Because, somewhere along the line, you gave up on tutoring. And I never really understood why."

It seems like the only thing that could have hurt him, and the main thing that sends his body into shock, is him remembering his relationship with Maya.

As fucked up as it sounds, it seems like a Wizard took advantage of a mentally ill man in his 20s, and broke him into his modern self in his early 30s.

Overall: Sekai probably dislikes Maya for what Maya did to Sensei mentally.

Not to mention, if Sekai is just some kind of hallucination from Sensei's mind, it might be the part of Sensei that regrets and dislikes what he did with Maya, personified. Just, you know, blaming the Wizard.

Could it have been her pushing to the "jump"? thus beginning some kind of infinite cycle for her to suffer for "breaking" the God's toy? That's why she can't touch him, it's Hell designed to make her suffer i guess.

Just wanted to chime in and say it's definitely possible that Maya has something to do with Sensei jumping.

In the 'Baby Finches' Happy Event, it ends with her trying to stop Sensei from jumping:
View attachment 3342912 View attachment 3342914 View attachment 3342915 View attachment 3342918 View attachment 3342920 Maya - "STOP!"
- "SENSEI!"
- "PLEASE!"

We've also had her mention wishing:

- 'This is not what I wished for!"
And in the first Reset she refers to this world as hers and Sensei's:
View attachment 3342938 Maya - "This is our world. We can do whatever we want in it."

Of course, she's narcissistic, so like Sensei, she'd probably just assume everything revolved around them.

There is however, apparently, an unexplained god at Maya's shrine:
View attachment 3342947 View attachment 3342970 View attachment 3342992 Yasu - "Then why do you reek of a shrine?"
Sensei - "Second, shrines don't have a scent."
Yasu - "But gods do. And I am very very very very very very very very very very very good when it comes to sniffing out things like that, Sensei."
Definitely hoping for some new information on her in the next update.

Also Tsuneyo may be some kind of bodyguard for USER2/The Wire god/The Calm god which may be her father. Tsuneyo has a strange affinity for killing feathered creatures which seems related to the Callous god, HOPE:
View attachment 3343046 View attachment 3343047 Tsuneyo - "Roll for initiative. Ram does not like the attitude the bird person is taking and has an advantage on attacks against all feathered creatures."
HOPE - "I AM THE THING WITH FEATHERS"
And hates Spiders, which seems related to the Concerned god, Pareidolia:
View attachment 3343067 View attachment 3343076
Tsuneyo - "No. My father just doesn't like spiders."
- "Fine. One more time. And I will keep my mouth shut even if I do have an immense distaste for arachnids."
Pareidolia's relation to Spiders:
And doesn't trust those who want Trust, which also seems related to the Concerned god, Pareidolia:
View attachment 3343084 View attachment 3343164 View attachment 3343167 Tsuneyo - "You are no more reliable than I am...but you want to be seen that way. And the people who want trust the most are, more often than not, the ones who are not meant to be trusted."
Pareidolia - "you have to trust me."
- "but i ask for your trust, and, should that trust be received, what you will gain in exchange for it shall be unrivaled."

Overall: If I were to sum up the god related girls, I'd probably sum it up like this:
  • Yasu - HOPE'S/The Callous god's Messenger. (Angel in Training)
  • Tsuneyo - The Wire god's/The Calm god's Guardian. (Flavour Samurai)
  • Kaori - Pareidolia's/The Concerned god's Mole. (Mistress of the Dark.)
Yasu goes around speaking on her god's behalf.

Tsuneyo has drawn a knife when Sensei got too close to her father, and she's more or less trained to kill and protect if it comes to it.

Kaori is working and trying to work everywhere in Kumon-mi, as well as getting a Chicken which should be HOPE's thing, and she completely ignored Maya who Pareidolia seems to intentionally get rid of, and befriends Ami who seems related to HOPE. Not to mention, befriending Sensei. She's somehow everywhere, yet Maya had no idea who she was when they recently met.

Edit: Kaori also just happens to be around the characters who see things. Sana and Sara, Ami and Sensei, and she's tried to get around Tsuneyo but Tsuneyo doesn't like her. Doesn't stop Kaori from creeping around the Ramen Shop, though.

posts.content_html_raw:
Speaking of rooms that ring bells, the mind space where Sensei was during his coma reminds me a lot of the end of Nodoka's book.
With the background behind Futaba being THE room with clocks, I suppose that is where her book ends instead of whatever I am thinking.

However, what tickles me is that, the ending of the book "The Light of Last Summer" in fact sounds pretty much like where we are now, a new chapter that moves on from a long ass summer and enters the infinite spring. Since her work is supposed to be the first installment of a new series, I don't think the end of that book is the end of LiL, but the end of the current harem phase, a phase that ends with Sensei starting hiding in a mind space full of clocks, seemingly abrupt and all of a sudden from the perspective of the unaware.

(plus I think making Nodoka too omnipotent is a weird story direction; being able to "access" how the current phase ends is still ok in my book but being able to access how everything ends? She might as well join Long Maya et al and become a full-time plot device, but that's me being personal and thinking out loud LOL)

Reminds me of some confusion I had about the similarities between something Tsubasa said in "Playing God" and something a narrator said during the first beach event in "See You in the Morning".



Initially, I figured that the narrator during this part of the beach event was Akira's memories of talking to Tsubasa in a previous timeloop. I thought it was interesting since the conversation with Tsubasa happened at some point after Maya mentioned that Akira never made it that far. It would imply that Maya's memories were also manipulated or reset before (like Tsuneyo mentions later).

However, if we start comparing Tsubasa with Sekai (or atleast consider some external factor influencing what Tsubasa says or how Akira hears it), then it opens some new options.
It could be that it mirrors a conversation from before the timeloop, although that would raise the question about with who that conversation was, and what makes it important to repeat it.
Since the talk of the narrator transitions into talk about being a tree, it could also be that it was a message from Wires, although that would still raise the question about the importance of the message and imply that Tsubasa is in some way related to Wires.

I'm probably looking too much into something that is not important, but if anyone has some idea/theory, I would be interested in knowing.

Fluffguck said:
To clarify a common misconception, no, no one gets banned from our discord just for existing here, and anyone who comes in here pretending they were probably knows exactly what they were banned for and doesn't want to admit it in public like this nazi here.
Click to expand...
Funny Nazi story - it's always nice to see real assholes face consequences - but make no mistake, I was banned in the Discord because of one post I made here offering the slightest pushback to Selly's behavior in a joking way - which I know because it was at a point when I hadn't been active in any Discords in a number of weeks.

After that point, when I started offering fair criticism of his behavior here in a way that wasn't just trying to laugh it off, he straight up lied about me having been "reprimanded" somehow for a dumb but completely benign joke I made almost a year prior, in order to respond to my criticism with a petty ad hominem attack.

Just so we're clear, I made a timeline for you. Forgive me for still keeping track, but I still find this to be a fascinating case study of some of the potential pitfalls of crowdfunding independent creators, and if this game wasn't the way it was, I could have made some cash out of a Youtube video on the story, given it's so incredible.

The ongoing state of play:
  • LiL has completely stagnated in support growth for more than half of the time it's been in development at this point.
  • This is literally unique among games that are still 1) very regularly updated, 2) with significant amounts of new content that 3) has remained somewhat consistent in quality.
  • For a multitude of very obvious reasons, it's clear this has had a negative impact on Selly's mindset and by extension, the quality of the game, given he refuses to let anyone else work on even the parts he hates doing, like animations and headpats.
Why?
  • This all started with the loss of Patreon, after the following sequence of events:
    • Selly treated a long-time patron poorly, who got butthurt and reported the game to Patreon. There were plenty of games at higher and lower revenues that broke TOS on Patreon at the time - games were not being actively monitored then like they are now
    • Patreon placed the page under review and gave Selly a second chance, which was objectively quite nice of them, given, you know, the entire nature of the game being very clearly and fundamentally against their TOS
    • Selly used this second chance to spend months on the Huggy Boy remake, which was such a ridiculous and stupid bad-faith parody of not only itself, but Patreon altogether, that it seemingly only served to insult the intelligence of the Patreon staff he was working with, because:
    • Patreon's TOS has always been clear that they don't allow games that have TOS-breaking content available as patches outside of the platform - something the characters in the Huggy Boy version explicitly stated, repeatedly, in their actual dialogue that anyone could read on-screen in a series of constant fourth-wall breaks
    • Predictably, he lost the use of the platform. Worst of all, they personally slighted him by not taking the time and effort to explain that it was because he was intentionally subverting their policies. LiL's days on it were obviously always going to be numbered, but he chose to go out by playing stupid games and winning stupid prizes, and I don't think many of his patrons appreciated it
  • Selly's continued takeaway from this experience is that Patreon were the ones who didn't understand their own TOS or train their employees properly, and Patreon were the ones who personally fucked him over. (Source: a rant by Sana that remains in the game to this day explicitly explaining exactly this)

    • But he did show some restraint. The memes insinuating putting the staff here to death for their purported crimes of treason "hypocrisy" and "selective rule enforcement" were kept in the Discord server - and it was all done with anime girls and cartoon swords anyway, so of course it was just playful and didn't mean anything, and me even bringing it up makes me a pussy, of course...

Initially, I figured that the narrator during this part of the beach event was Akira's memories of talking to Tsubasa in a previous timeloop. I thought it was interesting since the conversation with Tsubasa happened at some point after Maya mentioned that Akira never made it that far. It would imply that Maya's memories were also manipulated or reset before (like Tsuneyo mentions later).

However, if we start comparing Tsubasa with Sekai (or atleast consider some external factor influencing what Tsubasa says or how Akira hears it), then it opens some new options.
It could be that it mirrors a conversation from before the timeloop, although that would raise the question about with who that conversation was, and what makes it important to repeat it.
Since the talk of the narrator transitions into talk about being a tree, it could also be that it was a message from Wires, although that would still raise the question about the importance of the message and imply that Tsubasa is in some way related to Wires.

I'm probably looking too much into something that is not important, but if anyone has some idea/theory, I would be interested in knowing.
Click to expand...
Well, I do have a Theory about the Tsukiokas, but it isn't quite concrete yet.

In the 'Somewhere Far From Here' Chapter 3 Main Event (before the 2 month Time Skip to Beachmas that lead to Sekai's restoration), we had Yasu implying the Tsukioka estate shouldn't exist:
Yasu - "The way this steel box moves is wrong. It's as if it's going backwards...inching closer and closer to what should not belong. To what should not exist."

Yasu also mentions an interference that seems related to the Beach:
Yasu - "It is an interference. "
- "But if I listen closely... I can hear the ocean."

Taking into account Sekai is restored at the Beach soon afterwards, seems to have plans for Yasu, and Yasu then warns Sensei about things that shouldn't exist in her 'Hand of god' Chapter 3 Event (which happens to be where Sensei ended up back during Beachmas if Sekai puppeteers him, Futaba, and Makoto):
Sekai - "Well, aren't you the cutest little thing?"
Sensei - "I blink and wind up in a somewhat familiar place --- filled with memories that may be good for me but not so much for others."
Yasu - "What I am saying is that you should not get too close to that which does not exist --- for it is a greater danger to you than anything else you could ever imagine."
- "This world is a wonderful one, but there are things trying to exist here that simply shouldn't."

It seems likely that Sekai and The Tsukiokas may be related, and possibly shouldn't exist. (There's also how the Tsukiokas seem inexperienced with the World which may be a rich trope, but could also simply be because they actually haven't existed that long.)

Then the fact Yasu has ended up more or less adopted by the Tsukiokas, seems very suspicious to me.

Frankly, it seems like the Tsukiokas have adopted the Summer (Callous) god's girl (Yasu), and have been taking in the Old District girls like Chika and Chinami who may be related to the Winter (Calm) god, while giving Sensei a fuckable married mother figure, like Sekai (Tsubasa), a best friend support system that cares about him, like Niki (Touka), and a bossy wizard that he will tutor, like Maya (Tsukasa).

We've also seen Touka wearing a Butterfly Hairpin which is something Sekai usually wears:

And there's how Yasu implies Autumn colors are Red and Yellow:
Yasu - "Picture it! The reds and yellows of the fall! The pinks and blues of springtime! It is as if color itself has been taken from us!"
Sekai is red. The Tsukiokas are all shades of Yellow if you look at their name colors.

Overall: It seems like the Tsukiokas are related to Sekai, who may be The World Itself, and although not confirmed, may be the Autumn/Fall god and possibly USER4.

I could definitely be wrong, but I think the Tsukiokas and the World Itself/Sekai will play important roles in the near future.

Anyway, it seems like Sekai may be a Narrator:
Sekai(?) - "Rapist! Lecher! Pedophile! Flay her 'till she's DEAD! The things they'd say if only they could see inside my head."
Sensei - "It won't. That won't happen. Who are you?"
Sekai (?) - "A ghost!"
Seems related to the Beach, where the Narrator said that stuff, and seems related to Tsubasa who said that stuff later.

So, Tsubasa saying this may be another hint at her side in things.

vehemental said:
  • Then there's the DRM.
    • One notable example of how to implement DRM in an indie game is from Heartbound, by, funnily enough, a company called Pirate Software (named so I'm sure to poison search results of people trying to pirate their games). If you pirate it, a scuffed sea shanty with a "Yarr!" starts playing and a little dialogue popup keeps showing up encouraging you to tweet a screenshot of the "bug" on the screen to the developer so he can laugh at you. It's a little aggro towards people for whom $5-10 is a lot of money, but you know, whatever.
    • The way DRM was implemented in LiL was not a funny joke. It's not a proselytizing diatribe intended to sway the opinion of the user and convince them to gib Selly money. The girls don't start ignoring Sensei or rejecting his advances in the latest scenes. Ami doesn't mysteriously become the only girl who shows up in class and steers Sensei away from the series of blood trails leading to a dumpster, with the game closing with her thanking the player for not paying $5 so they could be together forever. Sensei doesn't even get locked in an inter-dimensional liminal space with the Tentacle Fuck Machine for the rest of eternity.
      • There are an infinite number of ways DRM could have been implemented in this game with no or even moderate levels of malice behind them, that could have even been consistent with the universe and maybe even funny(!) - but doing so would have taken some amount of additional effort and some amount of self-awareness that not all of the people who would fall victim to it are the dirty pirates on F95Zone "trying to run this game into the ground" from his perspective.
      • Instead, it was designed to be as vindictive and malicious as possible without running into actual legal trouble, and newer players who wanted the most content and didn't keep up with the game were always going to be affected the most, because the people following this thread were tipped off that the DRM was coming.
        • Side note for further irony: newer players, who have avoided the mountain of baggage surrounding a dev and who want the most content, are by far the most likely to become new supporters of a game that has a dev with a mountain of baggage surrounding him.
      • I know this is all bleeding-heart shit, but when you delete all the saves of this game, you're wiping out 50-100+ hours of effort on the part of the player, which is quite a bit for a potential "lost revenue" of $5 by the developer.
    • From my perspective, on the day the update with the DRM came out, as one of the people who was specifically waiting for it so we could crack the DRM (because we knew that Selly was going to go scorched earth mode and hurt his playerbase) - I had to adopt the role of a fan of a game who wanted to protect members of the game's fanbase from the depredations of the game's own developer, in the interest of that developer not continuing to shoot his own future success in the foot. I have never been in a more ridiculous situation in my life. This shit is a comedy sketch. It's absurdist and surreal.
Click to expand...
Fluffguck, I completely forgot to bring up the DRM in my first post, so I added a bit more context for you to hopefully not conveniently ignore. Hopefully you stick around, I don't think very many of the people who actively hate Selly are around anymore. It's a weird and unhealthy mindset to have over a silly porn game anyway.

DeSkel15 said:
Well, I do have a Theory about the Tsukiokas, but it isn't quite concrete yet.

In the 'Somewhere Far From Here' Chapter 3 Main Event (before the 2 month Time Skip to Beachmas that lead to Sekai's restoration), we had Yasu implying the Tsukioka estate shouldn't exist:
View attachment 3360794 Yasu - "The way this steel box moves is wrong. It's as if it's going backwards...inching closer and closer to what should not belong. To what should not exist."

Yasu also mentions an interference that seems related to the Beach:
View attachment 3360797 View attachment 3360798 View attachment 3360799 Yasu - "It is an interference. "
- "But if I listen closely... I can hear the ocean."

Taking into account Sekai is restored at the Beach soon afterwards, seems to have plans for Yasu, and Yasu then warns Sensei about things that shouldn't exist in her 'Hand of god' Chapter 3 Event (which happens to be where Sensei ended up back during Beachmas if Sekai puppeteers him, Futaba, and Makoto):
View attachment 3360808 View attachment 3360812 View attachment 3360820 View attachment 3360819 Sekai - "Well, aren't you the cutest little thing?"
Sensei - "I blink and wind up in a somewhat familiar place --- filled with memories that may be good for me but not so much for others."
Yasu - "What I am saying is that you should not get too close to that which does not exist --- for it is a greater danger to you than anything else you could ever imagine."
- "This world is a wonderful one, but there are things trying to exist here that simply shouldn't."

It seems likely that Sekai and The Tsukiokas may be related, and possibly shouldn't exist. (There's also how the Tsukiokas seem inexperienced with the World which may be a rich trope, but could also simply be because they actually haven't existed that long.)

Then the fact Yasu has ended up more or less adopted by the Tsukiokas, seems very suspicious to me.

Frankly, it seems like the Tsukiokas have adopted the Summer (Callous) god's girl (Yasu), and have been taking in the Old District girls like Chika and Chinami who may be related to the Winter (Calm) god, while giving Sensei a fuckable married mother figure, like Sekai (Tsubasa), a best friend support system that cares about him, like Niki (Touka), and a bossy wizard that he will tutor, like Maya (Tsukasa).

We've also seen Touka wearing a Butterfly Hairpin which is something Sekai usually wears:
View attachment 3360874 View attachment 3360877

And there's how Yasu implies Autumn colors are Red and Yellow:
View attachment 3360896 Yasu - "Picture it! The reds and yellows of the fall! The pinks and blues of springtime! It is as if color itself has been taken from us!"
Sekai is red. The Tsukiokas are all shades of Yellow if you look at their name colors.

Overall: It seems like the Tsukiokas are related to Sekai, who may be The World Itself, and although not confirmed, may be the Autumn/Fall god and possibly USER4.

I could definitely be wrong, but I think the Tsukiokas and the World Itself/Sekai will play important roles in the near future.

Anyway, it seems like Sekai may be a Narrator:
View attachment 3360945 View attachment 3360951 View attachment 3360959 View attachment 3360963 View attachment 3360966 Sekai(?) - "Rapist! Lecher! Pedophile! Flay her 'till she's DEAD! The things they'd say if only they could see inside my head."
Sensei - "It won't. That won't happen. Who are you?"
Sekai (?) - "A ghost!"
Seems related to the Beach, where the Narrator said that stuff, and seems related to Tsubasa who said that stuff later.

So, Tsubasa saying this may be another hint at her side in things.
Click to expand...
That's interesting. I do remember Imani wears the same butterfly hairpin but she's also more associated with blue. With the Nakayamas being pink and associated with spring, I think there must be some connection there and it's getting the wheels spinning. Imani's burns and backstory, spring's themes of restoration, it being the last unvisited season and Noriko restoring Akira's memories I feel like there's something there. With Autumn representing death and decay, all the past events with Maya and a broken Sensei it would contrast with Spring.

Perhaps some foreshadowing that our last season will be one of rebirth after the dark route is finally over. I'm not sure though, I feel like there's something there but it's just out of reach.

Wardtnaci said:
I've been thinking about this for a while now and with the last update there might be some validity to it....

I've been wondering if every pair of girls in each dorm room suffer from the same disorder; mental, physical, or Something else that the 2 similarly share. For Example:

These are apparent to me...
Dorm 8: Both Nodoka and Otoha have random bouts of mania.
Dorm 7: Both Uta and Io were lured, and possibly sexually abused, by online predators.
Dorm 4: Both inflict self harm. Futaba's bulimia to lose weight & Rin's cutting to snap out of her depression.
Dorm 2: Both Ayane and Sana have a Parent that suddenly walked out on them/family for no obvious reason.

These not so much...
Dorm 10: Kirin and Noriko may have something to do with their sisters and how they shaped themselves in reaction to their sisters
Dorm 9: Touka and Yasu have something to do with having a sheltered upbringing, but due to dissimilar circumstances.

Dorms 1, 3 & 6 nothing comes to mind yet.

With the last update I think both Ami and Maya in Dorm 5 have a mental disorder that has Isolation, a need to control their significant other(Akira) and Abandonment issues as symptoms. Caused by a Traumatic event(s) in their youth.

What does everybody or anybody think of this? Feel free to add to this or tear it apart. -cough- -cough- DeSkel15 -Cough- -Cough-!
Click to expand...
I can't speak for the disorders, but each dorm pair do have certain traits they share, imo.

For Dorm 1, 3, and 6:

Dorm 1 Chika and Yumi - Both have shown to be delusional and desire security. Overlooking the reality of things to have peace of mind. (Chika forces herself to see Sensei as Perfect, and Yumi has done things like convince herself she followed Sensei out of pity:
Yumi - "Just fucking...come with me if you need to talk to me that desperately. I don't want people to think the two of us are friends."
- "You're lucky I pitied you enough to follow you out here."
Sensei - "Does she really not remember that she's the one who led me?..."
She seems to rewrite what actually happens in her mind to make herself feel better.)

Dorm 3 Makoto and Miku - Both seem kind of trapped in the past. Like their mental development was damaged by their childhood. Miku due to what happened to her parents, Makoto due to the abnormal environment she grew up in.

Dorm 6 Molly and Tsuneyo - Fear of being unable to protect those they care about. (Molly was worried about Rin's cutting and was so glad that they checked on her, and Tsuneyo made it clear she'd execute Sensei if he rapes someone, after what he did to Molly.)

Other Dorms:
Dorm 2 Ayane and Sana - Both have shown to put up a facade to hide their true feelings, and presumably hate themselves for having them. (Ayane hates admitting weakness, and Sana has mentioned disliking mirrors:
Sana - "Plus...I don't really like mirrors...so.."
- "It's...kind of personal, so...if you don't mind..."
And frankly, her rape fetish may be due to feeling like she deserves to be abused.)

Dorm 4 Futaba and Rin - Both irrationally hate themselves and are dependent upon others to find worth in themselves. This is rather clear with Futaba, but Rin hates herself so much that she finds those like her (Molly and Rika) unattractive, and she seems to mostly just want to date, so that she can convince herself she's wanted by someone. Hence the whole need Otoha to want her stuff:
Rin - "I have to be wanted. I need her to want me. I can't lose her now, Sensei. I can't. I can't. I can't. I can't."

Dorm 5 Ami and Maya - Extreme fear of abandonment and change, which results in them having to be the best at their roles.

Dorm 7 Io and Uta - Both feel undesirable due to their past and who they are. Uta feels like a whore. Io feels like a burden.

Dorm 8 Nodoka and Otoha - Both seem to have trouble with Empathizing. They don't seem to truly understand emotions, especially those of others. This perhaps causes their manic episodes as they have trouble evoking the feelings they want in their work.

Dorm 9 Touka and Yasu - Both allow themselves to be tools for a higher power. Yasu has her god. Touka has her family name. Their own lives mean little in the face of this, and they find it difficult socializing with those different than them, due to this. They are followers, willingly letting themselves be used by that which is bigger than them.

Dorm 10 Kirin and Noriko - Both have let others define their lives. Their sisters indirectly forced them to be different than them. Kirin became the trouble maker, and Noriko tried becoming the dream girl of her sister's ex, both becoming who they did, to be noticed by the same people who noticed their sisters. They also seem kind of stuck in this character they've become, whether it makes them happy or not.

One question, what motivates you all to continue playing this game?

Is it boredom, curiosity about what's coming, any specific character? I'm curious about this.
Click to expand...
Honestly a variety of things keep me coming back, but I'll list the ones that come to mind:

- The characters (because come on). They're extremely well written and each have at least something about them that makes you want to grow closer to them and learn more about them.
- The lore. Okay yeah, it can be a confusing fucking mess a lot of the time, but ya know what? At least it's confusing in an... interesting way? What I mean when I say 'lore' obviously has to do with the history of the gods, the resets, and pieces of the puzzle in Sensei's past that we simply don't have yet. I genuinely like reading the theories on here and hope to one day solve the mysteries of the game for good.
- Akira's redemption. Is it a stretch to call it a redemption? Because yeah, he's not a good person by any stretch of the imagination, but you can't deny he's come a long way since Chapter 1. The more of his memories and past he attains, the more he's able to connect with people and showcase feelings such as guilt and empathy, such as with Maya, Ami, Ayane, Niki, etc. Akira can only grow from here, right? Especially now that he no longer has Maya Prime to lean on as a crutch. He's gonna have to step up to the plate and do some growing real soon.
- Maya, Noriko, Niki and Yumi. Yes that's a reason. Yes I know I'm technically repeating myself. Yes they're the best girls in the game.

I genuinely like reading the theories on here and hope to one day solve the mysteries of the game for good.
- Akira's redemption. Is it a stretch to call it a redemption? Because yeah, he's not a good person by any stretch of the imagination, but you can't deny he's come a
long
way since Chapter 1. The more of his memories and past he attains, the more he's able to connect with people and showcase feelings such as guilt and empathy, such as with Maya, Ami, Ayane, Niki, etc. Akira can only grow from here, right? Especially now that he no longer has Maya Prime to lean on as a crutch. He's gonna have to step up to the plate and do some growing real soon.
- Maya, Noriko, Niki and Yumi. Yes that's a reason. Yes I know I'm technically repeating myself. Yes they're the best girls in the game.

Then there is the issue of her claiming to be her guardian angel....
As for Nodoka, the theory that she could be related to Sensei comes to mind. Curiously, this event ends strongly with Nao rubbing Sekai's past in his face.

Matthew - "Probably last Christmas. Yuki makes an excellent Manhattan."
Sensei - "Wonderful. Thanks, Matthew."
Sara - "When did you meet Matthew?"
Sensei - "I can't really explain it, but I feel like he's always just kind of been there."
